title: Spontaneity and temperature: decomposing calcium carbonate
promptMarkdown:
Limestone decomposes on heating: $\ce{CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g)}$. Data at 298.15 K and 1 bar: $\Delta H^\circ_f$ (kJ mol⁻¹): $\ce{CaCO3(s)}$ −1207.6, $\ce{CaO(s)}$ −634.9, $\ce{CO2(g)}$ −393.5. $S^\circ$ (J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹): $\ce{CaCO3(s)}$ 91.7, $\ce{CaO(s)}$ 38.1, $\ce{CO2(g)}$ 213.8. $R = 8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$.

1. Compute $\Delta H^\circ_r$ and $\Delta S^\circ_r$, and say before calculating what sign you expect for $\Delta S^\circ_r$ and why.
2. Compute $\Delta G^\circ_r$ at 298.15 K. Is the decomposition spontaneous under standard conditions at this temperature?
3. Estimate the temperature above which the decomposition becomes spontaneous under standard conditions, and state the assumption this estimate requires.
4. Compute $K$ at 298.15 K and interpret it as an equilibrium pressure of $\ce{CO2}$ over the solids (which species appear in $K$ and which do not?). What is $K$ at the crossover temperature?
5. A learner says 'the reaction is endothermic, so it cannot happen'. Correct the statement in two sentences.
hintLadder: One mole of gas is produced from solids only; think about what that does to the number of microstates.
Convert $\Delta S^\circ$ to kJ K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ before forming $\Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ$.
$\Delta G^\circ = 0$ when $T = \Delta H^\circ/\Delta S^\circ$, provided both are treated as constants over the temperature range.
Pure solids have activity 1, so $K$ contains only the $\ce{CO2}$ pressure divided by 1 bar. $\ln K = -\Delta G^\circ/RT$ with $\Delta G^\circ$ in joules.

criteria.criterion: Distinguishes endothermicity from spontaneity: ΔG° can be negative above the conditional crossover, while actual direction at any temperature depends on CO₂ pressure through Q/K.

checkExamples.label: correct answer
checkExamples.text: ΔH° = (-634.9 - 393.5) - (-1207.6) = +179.2 kJ/mol. A gas is produced from solids, so ΔS° should be positive: 38.1 + 213.8 - 91.7 = +160.2 J/(K mol). ΔG°(298.15 K) = 179.2 - 298.15 x 0.1602 = +131.4 kJ/mol, not spontaneous. The crossover is T = 179200/160.2 = 1119 K, assuming ΔH° and ΔS° are independent of temperature. K = exp(-131400/(8.314 x 298.15)) = 9 x 10^-24 = P(CO2)/1 bar, since the two solids have activity 1; at the crossover K = 1. Endothermic reactions can be spontaneous once TΔS exceeds ΔH, so it is favourable under standard conditions above the conditional crossover; actual direction at any temperature depends on the CO2 pressure through Q/K.

checkExamples.label: unit slip and no assumption
checkExamples.text: ΔH° = 179.2 kJ/mol, ΔS° = 160.2 J/(K mol), so ΔG° = 179.2 - 298.15 x 160.2 = -47583 kJ/mol and the reaction is spontaneous; it becomes spontaneous above 1119 K.
